title: Cassoulet
subtitle: French slow-cooked white bean and pork casserole
excerpt: A long-simmered southern French casserole of white beans, pork belly, Toulouse sausages, and duck confit, finished with a golden breadcrumb crust. Rich, unctuous, and deeply satisfying.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cassoulet is the great slow-cooked dish of the Languedoc region of southern France. It takes its name from the cassole, the conical earthenware pot it is traditionally cooked in. There are three towns that each claim the definitive version: Castelnaudary (with pork and goose), Carcassonne (with lamb and partridge in season), and Toulouse (with Toulouse sausages and duck confit). The Toulouse version is the most widely made. The dish was originally a peasant stew, a way to cook dried beans with whatever preserved meat was available from the winter stores. The breadcrumb crust that forms on top is essential: it should be broken and pushed back into the casserole several times during cooking, thickening the beans and building up a deeply browned, flavourful crust.

recipeTools.notes: A large, deep oven-proof casserole dish.

content.text: Soak the beans overnight in cold water and cook them separately until just tender before assembling the cassoulet: undercooked beans will not soften properly in the oven. The breadcrumb crust should be broken back into the dish two or three times during baking, then left to form one final crust in the last 30 minutes. The finished dish should be thick and creamy, not soupy.

items.preparation: Toulouse or good herby pork sausages
confit or shop-bought confit; substitute 4 chicken thighs if unavailable

content.text: Cook the soaked, drained beans in a large pan of fresh water for 45 to 60 minutes until just tender. Drain and set aside.

Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Brown the pork belly and lardons in the oil in a large oven-proof casserole. Remove. Brown the sausages. Remove. Fry the onion for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato puree for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, thyme, and bay leaves.
Return the pork belly and lardons to the pot. Add the beans. Nestle the sausages and duck confit legs on top. The beans should be just submerged in liquid. Season with salt.
Scatter the breadcrumbs over the top. Bake for 1 hour 30 minutes. Break the crust back in twice during cooking. Leave the final crust intact for the last 30 minutes. Serve directly from the pot.
